issues.legal_issue: Land originally held as Watan property loses that character when the Government resumes it and dispenses with the hereditary service, unless the terms agreed upon preserve the Watan tenure.
material_facts: The disputed lands were originally Watan lands.
The Government had resumed the lands after dispensing with the service and levying full assessment.
The lands were described in the records as Japti Sanadi Inam lands, indicating that the grant had been resumed or confiscated and the lands left with the holder as ryotwari holdings.
The findings were that the hereditary office and the need to perform its service no longer existed.
There was no evidence of agreed terms preserving the Watan character of the lands.
The dispute came before the Court in a civil appeal concerning whether the lands retained their Watan character.
issues.conclusion: The lands had lost their Watan character and were ordinary ryotwari holdings; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 4 of the Bombay Hereditary Offices Act, 1874, a Watan comprises a hereditary office and any property assigned to remunerate its duties. Section 15 permits commutation of service on conditions agreed between the Collector and the holder; those conditions may preserve the Watan character, but do not necessarily do so. Section 22 contemplates that a Watan may lapse, be confiscated, or be lawfully resumed, and the Government may revoke a grant made to remunerate an abolished office. On resumption without terms preserving the tenure, the land reverts to ryotwari holding subject to land revenue assessment. The Court approved the conclusion in Ramijyabi Muktum Saheb v. Gudusaheb, 54 Bom. L.R. 405.

rule.if: civil_appeal_concerning_former_watan_land and land_was_resumed_or_confiscated and hereditary_service_was_dispensed_with and full_assessment_was_levied and no_terms_preserving_watan_character_were_shown

predicates.civil_appeal_concerning_former_watan_lan: The matter came before the court in a civil appeal concerning whether land formerly held as Watan property retained that status.
predicates.land_was_resumed_or_confiscated: The government resumed or confiscated the land that had previously been granted as Watan property.
predicates.hereditary_service_was_dispensed_with: The government dispensed with the hereditary service for which the land had been held.
predicates.full_assessment_was_levied: The government levied full ordinary assessment on the land.
predicates.no_terms_preserving_watan_character_were: The holder did not establish agreed terms that preserved the land's Watan character.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal concerns former Watan land and the government resumed it, ended the hereditary service, and levied full assessment, the land is an ordinary ryotwari holding if no agreed terms preserving its Watan character are shown.
